utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, we are now beginning the hearing. Would you please have the accused brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Be seated. First I would like to be sure that the interpreters are all ready, once the photographers have completed their work. Gentlemen? Fine. You can withdraw now, please. Does the interpreting booth hear me? Do my colleagues hear me? Prosecutor, and the Defence? Do the accused hear in their own language? We can now start the hearing, which, as I would like to say, is an initial appearance hearing, according to the International Criminal Tribunal's Statute. The Rules of Procedure state that an accused, after having had their indictment confirmed by a judge and after having been arrested and brought to the Tribunal, must go through a proceedings which is called the initial appearance. First, I will ask each of the accused to rise when his name is called and to state for the judges their name, first name, date and place of their birth and the names of their attorneys. First from left to right, Mr Pero Skopljak. Do you hear me? Please rise. Good morning. First give us your name. You have to turn your microphone on. We can hear you now. Please give us your name, your first name as well, where you live, the name of your attorney and your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SKOPLJAK
utterances.text: My name is Pero Skopljak, I was born on 4th June 1943 in Vitez. My attorney is Mrs Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Mr Santic, who according to the drawing that I have here should be the next one. Please sit down now, Mr Skopljak. Give me your name, Mr Santic, your name and the other information as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: My name is Ivan Santic, I was born on 30th July 1940 in Zenica, my attorney is Mr Ivan Kern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated. The next person, who should be Mr Cerkez, would you please rise, turn your microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: My name is Mario Cerkez, I was born on 27th March 1959, my attorney is Mr Ivan Kern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. And last, Mr Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: My name is Dario Kordic, I was born on 14th December 1960 in Sarajevo. I am married, my wife is called Renra, I have three children, Vladimir, Maria and Elizabeth. My attorney's name is Mrs Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I now turn -- please be seated first. After having asked the Registrar to call out the reference numbers for this case, this is what number now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case IT-95-14/2-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Dario Kordic, Mario Cerkez, Ivica Santic, Pero Skopljak, Zlatko Aleksovski and Tihofil Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr President, good morning your Honours, good morning counsel. My name is Mark Harmon, I will be appearing for the Prosecution this morning, and I will be assisted by Mr Gregory Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, would you introduce yourselves, please, and to recall which of the accused you are defending. Mrs Slokovic-Glumac, would you please spell your name for us; in any case, pronounce it clearly. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. My name is Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac, attorney, and I represent Mr Pero Skopljak and Mr Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: My name is Ivan Kern, attorney from Zagreb Croatia and I represent here Mr Mario Cerkez and Mr Ivan Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mrs Glumac, you did not indicate what bar you work with.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I am an attorney from Zagreb and a member of the Croatian Bar Association.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mrs Glumac and Mr Kern, did you indicate your qualifications and credentials to the Registry as far as your membership in the bar is concerned? Will you do that afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: We will be doing that in the next few days as we did not manage to collect all the necessary papers in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I did not hear Mr Kern's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: Mine have been handed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I suppose Mr Kern -- we still have not heard the French interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: We have handed in our authorisations and the other documents will be handed in soon. Our powers of attorney have been handed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. First, I would like to recall rapidly which of the Articles of the Statute govern this procedure. I would like to remind you that the Statute in Article 20, which was approved by the Security Council, states that the Trial Chamber shall read the indictment to satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instruct the accused to enter a plea. In Article 21, there are a series of rights which the accused are entitled to know of in a language which they understand, having to do with the nature and the reasons for the charges brought against them or against individuals. Specifically relating to the initial appearance, that is this hearing, we look at Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which were applied from the Statute, which have been voted on by the Security Council, which says that the Trial Chamber shall satisfy itself of the right of the accused to counsel; to read or have the indictment read to the accused in a language he speaks or understands; and satisfy itself that the accused understands the indictment and then call upon the accused to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count. Should the accused fail to do so, enter a plea of not guilty on his behalf, and last, in case of a plea of not guilty, instruct the Registrar to set a date for trial and we will speak about that in a little while. Should there be a guilty plea, to instruct the Registrar to set a date for the pre-sentencing hearing or any other appropriate dates. These are the rules governing this hearing. I would now like to turn to Mrs Glumac and to Mr Kern and to ask whether the accused that they are defending have received a copy of the indictment in a language which they understand, that is yours as well, and whether the accused understood what was in them before we read the indictment. First of all, then, Mrs Glumac, would you please answer this question, you who are defending Mr Skopljak and Mr Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honours, copies of the indictment have been handed to the accused and the accused have understood the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Kern?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the accused have received the indictment in their own language and they have understood the text handed to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. I will now ask the Registrar to read the entire indictment, including the two names that are the subject of proceedings already in progress. Registrar, would you please recall the date of the indictment and then read it, if you like?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is the indictment. The Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Dario Kordic, Tihofil also known as Tihomir Blaskic, Mario Cerkez, Ivan also known as Ivica Santic, Pero Skopljak, Zlatko Aleksovski. Indictment. Richard Goldstone, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to his authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia ("the Statute of the Tribunal") charges that: 1. Serious violations of international humanitarian law took place during the period of May 1992 to May 1993, when the armed forces of the Croatian Defence Council, (hereinafter referred to as HVO) of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna (hereinafter referred to as HZ-ZB) attacked the Muslim civilian population in the towns, villages and hamlets of the Lasva Valley area of Central Bosnia generally and specifically in the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca and the civilian population of the nearby city of Zenica, in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accused. 2. Dario Kordic, was born on 14th December 1960 in Sarajevo, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. From at least 1991 until the present, he has been an active and influential member of a Bosnian Croat political party named the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina (hereinafter referred to as HDZ BiH). From at least 22nd September 1992 until the present, he has been Vice-President and a member of the Presidency of HZ-HB and from on or about 10th July 1994, he has been Chairman of the HDZ BiH. 3. Tihofil Blaskic, son of Ivo, was born on 2 November 1960 in the village of Brestovsko, municipality of Kiseljak, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He is a career military officer, who graduated from the Military Academy in Belgrade in 1983 and formerly served as a Captain in the Yugoslav Peoples Army (JNA). At all times material to this indictment, he held the rank of Colonel and was the Commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone of the HVO. Since about August 1993, he has held the rank of General and is the Chief of Staff of the HVO with his headquarters in Mostar. 4. Mario Cerkez, son of Tugomir, was born on 27 March 1959 in the village of Rijeka, municipality of Vitez, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. His Official Personal Identification Number is 2703959193612. In 1992, during the formation of the HVO forces in Vitez, he became the commander of the HVO Brigade stationed in the municipality of Vitez. He held that position until at least the end of May 1993 and during the HDZBiH/HVO take-over of the municipal functions within Vitez municipality. He is currently residing in Vitez. 5. Ivan Santic, son of Stipe, was born in 1942 and is married to Marica. He is a chemical engineer and was formerly the Technical Manager of the Sintevit factory in Vitez. He was Mayor of the municipality of Vitez from at least May 1992 and at all times material to this indictment. He held this position during the HDZBiH/HVO take-over of the municipal functions within the Vitez municipality. He is currently residing in Vitez. 6. Pero Skopljak, son of Ante, was born on 4 June 1943 in Vitez, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. His Official Personal Identification Number is 0406943193610, and he was a graduate of the Faculty of Theology of the Roman Catholic Church. He was formerly the President of the Executive Committee of Vitez HDZBiH Electoral Assembly and Chief of Police, at the Public Security Station, of Vitez municipality in Central Bosnia from at least October 1992 to May 1993. He is now an official in the office of the Vice-President of HZ-HB. 7. Zlatko Aleksovski, son of Tale and Eva (nee Stanko), was born on 8 January 1960 in Pakrac, Pakrac municipality, in the Republic of Croatia. He completed studies at the "Veljko Vlahovic" Faculty of Political Sciences political sciences, Department of Sociology, in Sarajevo on 28 September 1983. From 23 February 1987, he was employed as a counsellor at the "Zenica Correction House" until on or about 29 January 1993, when he left to become commander of the prison facility at Kaonik, near Busovaca. After May 1993, he left Kaonik to become the Head of the District HVO "Heliodrom" prison in Mostar, which was also under the administration of the HZ-HB. Superior authority. 8. Dario Kordic was elected President of the HDZBiH party in the municipality of Busovaca in 1991. This party was the main Bosnian Croat political party in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. On 18 November 1991, he participated in the formation of the HZ-HB, and was a signatory to the decision establishing HZ-HB in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That Bosnian Croat political entity was proclaimed by the HDZBiH to include the municipalities of Travnik, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Busovaca and Kiseljak. By at least 10 May 1992, Kordic became the Vice-President of the HVO in HZ-HB. By at least 22 May 1992, he became at least one of two Vice-Presidents of HZ-HB, and remained so at all times material to this indictment. 9. Dario Kordic was, by virtue of his position as a Vice-President of HZ-HB, also a member of the Presidency, being the legislative body of HZ-HB. According to Article 7 of the Decision on Founding the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, dated 3 July 1992, its Presidency consists of the President, two Vice-Presidents and the Secretary. 10. Dario Kordic, by virtue of holding various political positions from time to time, culminating in his positions as Vice-President of HZ-HB and the HVO, and by virtue of his political power base in Central Bosnia, exerted power, influence and control over the political and strategic aims and operations of the HVO in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone (one of the four HVO military operative zones within HZ-HB) at all times material to this indictment. 11. Dario Kordic demonstrated power, influence, authority and control on numerous occasions and in numerous ways, including, but not limited to, negotiating cease-fire agreements, issuing orders that were directly or indirectly of a military nature, representing himself as a HVO Colonel, dressing in a HVO uniform, having a military operations room in his office in Busovaca, countermanding cease-fire agreements when the terms were not suitable to him, issuing orders for the arrest or release of influential Muslims held prisoner by the HVO and negotiating the passage of relief convoys or United Nations vehicles through checkpoints in Central Bosnia. 12. Tihofil Blaskic, since the establishment of the HVO on 8 April 1992, was instrumental in the implementation of the structure and functioning of the HVO in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. From at least May 1992, he was a Colonel in the HVO and the Commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and remained so at all times material to this indictment. Tihofil Blaskic's authority and duties as a commander are set forth in the Decree on the Armed Forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, dated 17 October 1992. That decree provides, inter alia, that he is responsible for the combat readiness of the troops under his command, the mobilisation of the armed forces and police units and the authority to appoint commanders. 13. Tihofil Blaskic has demonstrated or exercised his control in military matters in a variety of ways including, but not limited to, negotiating cease-fire agreements, negotiating with United Nations officials, establishing the organisational structures of the Armed Forces of the HVO, appointing and relieving military commanders, deploying troops, artillery and other units under his command, issuing orders to municipal HVO headquarters, acting as a liaison with senior Croatian Army officials and controlling external military units operating within his area of command. 14. Mario Cerkez, from at least August 1992, was the Commander of the HVO Brigade situated in the municipality of Vitez, and remained so at all times material to this indictment. His position within the HVO meant he came under the Command of Tihofil Blaskic, the HVO Central Bosnia Operative Zone Commander at the time. The "Viteska" Brigade headquarters was situated in the Hotel Vitez, the same building as Blaskic's headquarters. Mario Cerkez's authority and duties as a commander are set forth in the Decree on the Armed Forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, dated 17 October 1992, which provides, inter alia, that he is responsible for the combat readiness of the troops under his command, the mobilisation of the armed forces and police units, and the authority to appoint commanders. 15. Mario Cerkez has demonstrated or exercised his control in military matters in a variety of ways including, but not limited to, negotiating cease-fire agreements with opposing civil and military figures from within the Muslim community, negotiating with United Nations officials, appointing military commanders, issuing orders to deploy troops and other units under his command and controlling the detention and treatment of detained civilians during times of military conflict. 16. Ivan Santic was the Mayor of the municipality of Vitez from at least May 1992 until May 1993. He represented the Bosnian Croat population of Vitez within the HDZBiH. Democratic by virtue of his political and official position, he exerted considerable power, influence, authority and control over the political and strategic military aims of the HVO in the municipality of Vitez. 17. Ivan Santic has demonstrated or exercised his control over civil and military matters within the Vitez municipality in a variety of ways, including, but not limited to, negotiating cease-fire agreements with opposing civil and military figures from within the Muslim community, negotiating with United Nations officials, controlling the municipal and governmental functions within Vitez municipality and controlling the detention and treatment of detained civilians during times of military conflict. 18. Pero Skopljak was a President of the Executive Committee of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the municipality of Vitez from at least October 1992 to May 1993 he was the Chief of Police in the municipality of Vitez. By virtue of his political and official position, he exerted power, influence, authority and control over the political and strategic military aims of the HVO in the municipality of Vitez. 19. Pero Skopljak has demonstrated or exercised his control over civil, police and military matters within the municipality of Vitez in a variety of ways including, but not limited to, negotiating cease-fire agreements with opposing civil and military figures from within the Muslim community, negotiating with United Nations officials, controlling the municipal and governmental functions and controlling the detention and treatment of detained civilians during times of military conflict. 20. Zlatko Aleksovski was an official at the Zenica prison from 23 February 1987 until leaving to be the commander of the detention facility at Kaonik, near Busovaca, on or about 29 January 1993. He was in charge of Kaonik Prison and was in a position of superiority to everyone else in the camp. As commander he met the International Committee of the Red Cross (hereinafter referred to as the ICRC) and European Community Monitoring Mission (hereinafter referred to as ECMM) officials and provided them with lists of detained persons and acknowledged his position of commander of the facility and his understanding of the Geneva Conventions in relation to the detention and treatment of prisoners in his charge. 21 Zlatko Aleksovski has demonstrated or exercised his control over the detention facility in Kaonik prison in a variety of ways including, but not limited to, formal meetings with ICRC and ECMM officials, accepting the custody of arrested persons by HVO units, allowing the unlawful interrogation of detained persons and allowing them to be used for unlawful forced labour (digging trenches) and human shields. 22. General allegations: 22.1. At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of international armed conflict and partial occupation existed in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. 22.2. All acts or omissions herein set forth as grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 (hereafter "grave breaches"), recognised by Article 2 of the Statute of the Tribunal, occurred during that international armed conflict and partial occupation. 22.3. In each paragraph charging crimes against humanity, a crime recognised by Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, the alleged acts or omissions were part of a widespread, large-scale or systematic attack directed against the civilian population, specifically the Bosnian Muslim population of the Lasva Valley region of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 22.4. All of the victims referred to in the charges contained in this indictment were, at all relevant times, persons protected by the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 22.5. All of the accused in this indictment were required to abide by the mandate of the laws and customs governing the conduct of war, including the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 22.6. The general allegations contained in paragraphs 8 through 22.5 are re-alleged and incorporated into each of the related charges set out below. Charges: 23. Between 01 May 1992 and 31 May 1993, Bosnian Muslims were persecuted on political, racial and religious grounds throughout the Lasva Valley area. Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic, during those times, and throughout the Lasva Valley area, did, by their acts and omissions, and in concert with others, commit a crime against humanity by persecuting Bosnian Muslims on political, racial and religious grounds. They are criminally responsible for the murder and wounding of Muslim civilians or detainees, the attacking and bombarding of undefended towns, villages and dwellings, deliberate attacks on the civilian population, the unlawful destruction of businesses, homes, personal property and livestock, the unlawful treatment of detainees, the targeting of political leaders and professionals by murdering them or detaining them in detention facilities for extended periods of time, the plundering of homes and personal property, the transferring or forcing of civilians to move out of the Lasva Valley to predominantly Muslim populated regions and the commission of other inhumane acts. Persecution was carried out by one or more of the aforementioned means, some of which are more particularised below. 24. In January and April 1993, HVO forces or their agents, under the direction and control of Dario Kordic and Tihomir Blaskic, planned and executed a systematic campaign of bombarding, attacking and destroying towns, villages and hamlets in the Lasva Valley area, or parts thereof, whose inhabitants were predominantly Bosnian Muslims. These communities, and their Bosnian Muslim inhabitants, were selected and targeted on political, racial and religious grounds. The attacks on these communities were conducted by HVO forces, which in the Vitez municipality included members of the Viteska Brigade, under the direction and control of Mario Cerkez. The Bosnian Muslim communities that were attacked in the Lasva Valley area had few or no Bosnia and Herzegovina Army troops (hereinafter referred to as BiH) troops present or near the community. Many of the attacks commenced early in the morning when most of the inhabitants were in their homes and asleep. At least one hundred defenceless Bosnian Muslim civilians, including women, children, the elderly and the infirm, were killed and many wounded or harmed in their homes, in their yards, while attempting to escape from the HVO attacks or bombardments or after they had been detained by the HVO. 25. In late April 1993, when the ABiH forces were involved in a counter-offensive against the HVO in or near the Lasva Valley area, HVO forces or their agents, under the direction and control of Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic, bombarded civilians gathering in the central shopping area of Zenica, resulting in the deaths of at least 17 civilians and the wounding of many others. 26. Between 1 January and at least 31 May 1993, in the municipalities of Busovaca and Vitez, hundreds of Bosnian Muslim civilians that had not escaped from or been killed in HVO attacks, were systematically selected and rounded up on political, racial or religious grounds by HVO forces or their agents, under the direction and control of Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic. These Bosnian Muslims civilians, including the many wounded in the attacks, were taken and detained by HVO forces or their agents, some of which included members of the Viteska Brigade, which was under the direction and control of Mario Cerkez. These civilians were interned, along with captured Muslim combatants, in detention facilities located at diverse locations in the Lasva Valley area. These facilities include, but are not limited to, the Vitez Cinema Complex, the Kaonik Prison near Busovaca, the Vitez Veterinary Station, the Dubravica Elementary School, and several Muslim homes in Gacice. 27. These detention facilities were staffed, operated or controlled by the HVO or their agents, under the direction and control of Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic. 28. The hundreds of Bosnian Muslim civilians described in paragraph 26, were detained in these facilities for various lengths of time on the basis of political, racial and religious grounds until they were either killed, transferred or forced to move to Muslim dominated areas outside the Lasva Valley area generally, and specifically outside the municipalities of Vitez, Novi Travnik and Busovaca. 29. While detained, many of the Muslim civilians and captured Muslim combatants were subjected by the HVO or their agents, under the direction and control of Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic, to inhumane treatment, including being kept in cramped or overcrowded facilities, being provided with inadequate food or water, being provided with inadequate or no medical treatment for the infirm or wounded, being subjected to physical or psychological abuse and intimidation, being repeatedly forced to dig trenches for the HVO at numerous and diverse locations at or near lines of confrontation between the HVO and the ABiH, thereby subjected such detainees to mental and physical harm, being subjected to use as human shields at diverse locations in the Lasva Valley area in order to protect HVO military installations or troops from forces hostile to the HVO and some being shot or beaten to death by the HVO. 30. On 19 April 1993, Mario Cerkez, having previously controlled the arrest and detention of hundreds of Muslim civilians through his command of HVO units in Vitez, stated that the HVO would kill the 2,200 Muslim civilians detained in Vitez unless pressure was put on the ABiH and civilian authorities to stop the ABiH counter-offensive in the Vitez area. This threat was reaffirmed on 20 April 1993 by Pero Skopljak and Ivan Santic and they were thus able, through threats, intimidation and coercion, to force the signing of a document beneficial to the interest of the HVO and potentially detrimental to the interests of the ABiH. Thereafter, Mario Cerkez, Pero Skopljak and Ivan Santic, allowed the continued detention of the Muslim civilian detainees who were under their care and control, the inhumane treatment of the detainees, the use of detained persons for forced labour (digging trenches) and the use of detained persons as human shields. During such time of detention some of them were murdered or otherwise killed. 31. From January 1993 until at least the end of May 1993, Zlatko Aleksovski accepted hundreds of detained Bosnian Muslim civilians from the HVO or their agents into his custody at the detention facilities in Kaonik. The detainees were from a widespread area including, but not exclusive to, Vitez and Busovaca municipalities. Many of the detainees under his control were subjected to inhumane treatment including, but not limited to, excessive and cruel interrogation, physical and psychological harm, forced labour (digging trenches), in hazardous circumstances, being used as human shields and some were murdered or otherwise killed. 32. Persecution, throughout the Lasva Valley area, involved the systematic and wanton destruction of Bosnian Muslim homes, personal property, livestock and businesses by the HVO armed forces, police, and their agents, or third parties with their acquiescence, under the direction or control of Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic. Between October 1992 and the end of May 1993, Bosnian Muslim property was singled out on the basis of political, racial and religious grounds and systematically destroyed, either before the hostilities commenced or during or after the HVO attacks on the Muslim civilian population in the Lasva Valley area. The effect of this unlawful, excessive and wanton destruction of hundreds of Bosnian Muslim homes, personal property and livestock, not justified by military necessity, was to ensure that the inhabitants who had not been killed, could not or would not return to their homes and communities in the Lasva Valley area. The towns, villages and hamlets, or Muslim portions thereof, where extensive destruction occurred, include, but are not limited to: Town/village: Ahmici, approximate period of destruction April 1993. Busovaca, January 1993 to May 1993. Gacice, April 1993. Kacuni, April 1993. Loncari, April 1993. Nadioci, April 1993. Ocenici, April 1993. Pirici, April 1993. Putis, April 1993. Santici, April 1993. Sivrino Selo, April 1993. Stari Vitez, April 1993. Veceriska/Donja Veceriska, April 1993. Vitez, December 1992 to May 1993. 33. Beginning in January 1993 and through to May 1993, HVO forces or their agents, under the direction or control of Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic, on the basis of political, racial and religious grounds, unlawfully bombarded the central shopping area of Zenica and systematically attacked hundreds of undefended dwellings or buildings in numerous towns, villages and hamlets in diverse locations in the Lasva Valley area that were owned, and many of which were occupied, by Bosnian Muslim civilians, and were of no military significance at the time of the attack or bombardment, in order to kill, terrorise, or demoralise the Bosnian Muslim population. These incidents resulted in hundreds of Bosnian Muslim casualties in numerous locations including, but not limited to: Ahmici, commencement date 16 April 1993, 5.30 am. Busovaca, January 1993 and 26 April 1993. Gacice, 20 April 1993, 5.50 am. Kacuni, January 1993. Loncari 17 April 199. Nadioci, 16 April 1993, 5.30 am. Ocenici, 19 April 1993. Pirici, 16 April 1993, 6.00 am. Putis, 16 April 1993. Santici, 16 April 1993, 5.30 am. Sivrino Selo, 16 April 1993. Stari Vitez 16 April 1993, 5.45 am. Veceriska/Donja Veceriska, 16 April 1993, 5.30 am, Vitez, 16 April 1993, 5.15 am, Zenica, 19 April 1993. 34. All events described in paragraphs 22 to 33 were directed against Bosnian Muslim civilians on political, racial and religious grounds. Individually and collectively, these actions were on such a large scale and widespread basis, and implemented in such a systematic fashion, that they have effectively destroyed or removed almost the entire Muslim civilian population from those areas of the Lasva Valley where the HVO and Bosnian Croat administration has taken control. Counts 1 to 3. Crimes against humanity. 35. Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic, between 1 May 1992 and 31 May 1993, individually, and in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation or execution of the following crimes: (a) persecutions of Bosnian Muslims in the Lasva Valley area of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, on political, racial and religious grounds, (b) bombardments and attacks which caused the deaths of over one hundred Bosnian civilians in the Lasva Valley area and the city of Zenica, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina,. (c) inhumane acts against Bosnian civilians in the Lasva Valley area, and civilians in the central shopping district of the city of Zenica, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and, or in the alternative, knew, or had reason to know, that subordinates were about to do the same, or had done so, and failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. By these acts and omissions Dario Kordic and Tihofil Blaskic: Count 1: a crime against humanity as recognised by Articles 5(h) (persecution on political, racial and religious grounds), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal (as described in paragraphs 24-25 which are incorporated in full herein); Count 2: a crime against humanity as recognised by Articles 5(a) (murder), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal (as described in paragraphs 24-25 which are incorporated in full herein); Count 3: a crime against humanity, as recognised by Articles 5(i) (inhumane acts), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal (as described in paragraphs 23, 28-34, and all references to the wounding or harming of many Bosnian civilians as set out in paragraphs 24-25, all of which are incorporated in full herein). Counts 4-7. Grave breaches and violation of the laws or customs of war. Wilful and killing and wounding of Bosnian Muslim civilians. 36. Dario Kordic, Tihofil Blaskic and Mario Cerkez, between 1 January and 31 May 1993, and as described in paragraphs 24-25 of this indictment, both of which are incorporated in full herein, individually, and in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of the murder of over one hundred civilians and the wounding of many others in the Lasva Valley area and in the city of Zenica, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and, or in the alternative, knew, or had reason to know, that subordinates were about to do the same, or had done so, and failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. By these acts or omissions, Dario Kordic, Tihofil Blaskic and Mario Cerkez, committed: Count 4: a grave breach as recognised by Articles 2(a) (wilful killing), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 5: a grave breach as recognised by Articles 2(c) (wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 6: a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Articles 3 (deliberate attack on the civilian population and individual civilians), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 7: a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) (murder) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. Counts 8-10, grave breaches and violation of the laws or customs of war. Unlawful treatment of Bosnian Muslim detainees. 37. Dario Kordic, Tihofil Blaskic, Mario Cerkez, Ivan Santic, Pero Skopljak and Zlatko Aleksovski, between 1 January and 31 May 1993, and as otherwise described in paragraphs 23 and 26-31 of this indictment, all of which are incorporated in full herein, individually, and in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation or execution of the unlawful treatment of Bosnian Muslim detainees in the Lasva Valley area of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and, or in the alternative, knew, or had reason to know, that subordinates were about to do the same, or had done so, and failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. By these acts and omissions, Dario Kordic, Tihofil Blaskic, Mario Cerkez, Ivan Santic, Pero Skopljak and Zlatko Aleksovski committed: Count 8: a grave breach as recognised by Articles 2(b) (inhumane treatment), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 9: a grave breach as recognised by Articles 2(c) (wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 10: a violation of the laws or customs of war (outrages upon the personal dignity) as recognised by Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Counts 11-13, grave breach and violations of the laws or customs of war. Attacks, bombardments and destruction of civilian property. 38. Dario Kordic, Tihofil Blaskic and Mario Cerkez, between 1 January and 31 May 1993 and otherwise as described in paragraphs 23-25 and 32-33 of this indictment, all of which are incorporated in full herein, individually, and in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation or execution of the unlawful attacking, bombarding, and destruction of Bosnian Muslim dwellings, businesses, buildings, personal property and livestock in the Lasva Valley area of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and, or in the alternative, knew, or had reason to know, that subordinates were about to do the same, or had done so, and failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. By these acts and omissions Dario Kordic, Tihofil Blaskic and Mario Cerkez committed: Count 11: a grave breach as recognised by Articles 2(d) (extensive destruction of property), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 12: a violation of the laws or customs of war (wanton destruction of dwellings or other installations that are used only by the civilian population, including places of religious worship) as recognised by Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Count 13: a violation of the laws or customs of war (attacks on dwellings or other installations that are used only by the civilian population, including places of religious worship) as recognised by Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Signed Richard Goldstone, Prosecutor, November 1995, The Hague, The Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to turn to the Defence attorneys and to their accused. Please note that this indictment was read in its entirety and, as you have noted, has two other names in it, Tihofil Blaskic and Zlatko Aleksovski. The reason for this is, as you know, Tihofil Blaskic and Mr Zlatko Aleksovski are being tried in separate procedures. Tihofil Blaskic's trial began about three or four months ago and Zlatko Aleksovski's will begin shortly. This is the reason for that. I first wanted to tell you this and to note it, because the judges want very much that the indictment be read exactly as it was drafted in November 1995, against the four accused. I ask the Defence attorneys whether they have understood exactly what I have just said, and I suppose your clients have also understood that; is that right? Now, I would like to turn to each of the accused and ask him whether he pleads guilty or not guilty to each of the counts in the entire indictment which has just been read. I will first ask Mr Dario Kordic to rise. Mr Kordic, you, of course, heard the indictment read in the language which is your own, and you have understood all the facts; would you answer yes or no? If you have anything you are not sure about, something which you did not understand, let me know, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen, I have fully understood the indictment and you said that I heard it in my language, that is not quite correct, because it was not in Croatian, I heard it more in Serbian, so that is the comment I have to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This comment, which was not the first time we have heard it, and which has already been settled here, will be noted in the transcript for this hearing. Mr Kordic, I am going to recall each of the counts which involves you, there are 13 which affect you. I will simply give the name and ask you to answer clearly whether or not you plead guilty. Count 1, crime against humanity, persecution for political, racial and religious reasons, Article 5(h) of the Tribunal Statute. Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 2, a crime against humanity, murder, Article 5(a) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 3, a crime against humanity, inhumane acts, Article 5(i) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 4, grave breach, wilful killing, Article 2(a) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 5, grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 6, violations of the laws and customs of war, deliberate attack on the civilian population and individual civilians, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Also not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 7, violation of the laws or customs of war, murder, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would prefer that you state whether you plead guilty or not. The interpretation said you do not "feel" guilty. In my language there is somewhat of a difference there. I would like you to say "I plead guilty" or "not guilty", if you do not mind. Count 8, grave breach, inhumane treatment, Article 2(b) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty. I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 9, grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 10, violations of the laws or customs of war, outrages upon personal dignity, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 11, grave breach, extensive destruction of property, Article 2(d) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 12, violation of the laws or customs of war, wanton destruction of dwellings or other installations used only by the civilian population, including places of religious worship, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 13, violations of the laws or customs of war, attacks on dwellings or other installations used only by the civilian population, including places of religious worship, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: Therefore I plead not guilty on all counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then this is the statement which has been recorded. Did you understand, in the language which you received, which you seemed to be challenging, at least the linguistic connotation of it? At least did you understand the indictment, Mr Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KORDIC
utterances.text: I have understood it completely, but I said that I would have preferred to have heard it in the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now Mr Mario Cerkez to rise. Please answer to each of the counts that were brought against you in the indictment which has just been read to you. Answer whether you plead guilty or not guilty. Count 4, wilful killing, Article 2(a) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 5, grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 6, violation of the laws or customs of war, deliberate attack on the civilian population and individual civilians, Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 7, violation of the laws or customs of war, murder, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 8, grave breach, inhumane treatment, Article 2(b) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 9, grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 10, violation of the laws or customs of war, outrages upon the personal dignity, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 11, grave breach, extensive destruction of property, Article 2(d) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 12, violation of the laws or customs of war, in this case wanton destruction of dwellings or other installations used only by the civilian population, including places of religious worship, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 13, violations of the laws or customs of war, attacks on dwellings or other installations used only by the civilian population, including places of religious worship, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore you are pleading not guilty to all of the counts which were brought against you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: I plead not guilty on all counts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have noted that. Have you also understood the indictment, Mr Cerkez? Did you understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I completely understood the indictment, and I plead not guilty on all counts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Cerkez. It will be noted as that and you may be seated. I would like to call Mr Ivan Santic. You are cited in this indictment. First I would like to ask you whether you understood the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understood them as they were written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is how it will be noted in the transcript. You understood what was written. Mr Santic, you are covered by three counts on this indictment. Count 8, grave breach, inhumane treatment, Article 2(b) of the Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 9, grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 10, violation of the wars or customs of war, outrage upon personal dignity, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Santic, you may be seated. It will be noted in that way in the transcript of this hearing that on the three counts which concern you, that is 8, 9 and 10, you plead not guilty. Mr Pero Skopljak, would you rise, please? First I ask you whether you heard and understood the indictment as it was read in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. SKOPLJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are covered by three counts in this indictment, Mr Skopljak, 8, 9 and 10. As for Count 8, grave breach, inhumane treatment, Article 2(b) of the Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. SKOPLJAK
utterances.text: I plead absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 9, grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, Article 2(c) of the Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. SKOPLJAK
utterances.text: I plead absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 10, violation of the laws or customs of war, outrages upon personal dignity, Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SKOPLJAK
utterances.text: I plead absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated, Mr Skopljak. Turning to the Registrar, would you please note all of the pleas, all of which were pleas of not guilty. I will now go into the last part of this hearing, which is the organisation of the Trial Chamber's work and the possible setting of a date for the trial. First, I will turn to the Prosecutor and remind him of his obligation which, according to Rule 66, is his, that he must give a copy of all -- make available to the Defence as soon as possible after the initial appearance copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought, as well as all prior statements obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor. You must understand now, Mr Prosecutor, that the Tribunal has been in existence for several years now, and in light of the case law which the Tribunal has been able to render in a number of cases which arose out of various preliminary comments and motions of the different accused -- Mr Prosecutor, have you any points you would like to comment on here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr President, we understand our obligations, we are in the process of preparing those materials for counsel and I hope to engage counsel in discussions in respect of some of those materials shortly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I suppose that you could not give the Defence a timeframe for when you will communicate this to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr President, I think we can communicate those materials to the Defence within two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mrs Glumac and Mr Kern, did you hear that? Within two weeks you will be entitled to have all of the documents that were attached to the indictment and the confirmation request which was presented by my colleague for the indictment which you have just heard, as well as the statements which were gathered. You understood things in that manner, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour and we hope this applies to the implementation of Rule 66A, and that we will receive all the supporting material and statements required under that rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: I have also understood it, I think that the deadline is a reasonable one and we hope it will be observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Kern, the Tribunal is here to be sure that these timeframes are respected. I would like to remind all parties, to Defence and to the Prosecution, that you have 60 days from today, 8th October 1997, the day of the initial hearing, to file any preliminary motions which are permitted under Rules 72 and 73 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The Prosecutor is familiar with these provisions, perhaps the Defence attorneys are less so. I therefore ask you to look at the text involved which refer to 60 days, but which can be extended by the Trial Chamber if it so decides, but only in an intraparty hearing. Before we leave, we must set up a date for a Status Conference in order to look at the status of the work and to settle any problems before we set a date for the trial. I must also point out to you that there are a certain number of things and questions which I feel responsible about and must tell you. For the time being, we have only one courtroom. This is a problem the Tribunal is confronted with and which must be settled during 1998. I do not know whether there will be any questions happening with any questions of possible separation of trials, only you can make those requests, or not make any. I would tell you that the composition of the Trial Chamber may change. You know that the Tribunal is finishing its first mandate given to it by the Security Council on 17th November. After that date, the composition of the trial will change for six of us judges. Therefore, there may be a modification in the Trial Chamber's composition. I simply wanted to point this out to you. If there are any other questions? Mrs Glumac, Mr Kern, have you any comments that you would like to make about this hearing?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the present, I have no further comments to make and until we receive the supporting material, we cannot make any further submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Kern?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERN
utterances.text: Yes, we have understood our rights and we will avail ourselves of those rights when we receive all the supporting material attached to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Turning to the Prosecutor, have you any comments that you would like to make as to the conduct of the work? I say this for the Defence as well. Access to the Trial Chamber is easy, Mr Fourmy is the legal officer in this Trial Chamber, through whom you can communicate anything you would like, in order to speak to the judges, or to communicate with them. Mr Harmon, do you have any additional comments you would like to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I now turn to my colleagues. Mr Karibi-Whyte, have you any comments you would like to make?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen, have you any comments you would like to make?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No comments at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Turning to the Registrar, are we in a position now to set a trial date? As things stand now, I believe this would be difficult, but I would like to have your opinion in order to comply with all the provisions of the text which apply to our work.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be difficult to give you a trial date now, to suggest a trial date to you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Registrar. If there are no other comments, the hearing is adjourned and will resume for a Status Conference.
